## Findings
- claim-1: Bigrassmannians \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) satisfy \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) and \(t>r+s-n\); their parameters are \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 187-235]
- claim-2: A valid tuple requires \(n,r,i,j,a,b,N\ge1\), \(r<n\), \(a+j\le r\), \(a+i\le n-r\), \(b\le i,j\), and \(N\le ab\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 300-304]
- claim-3: Put \(q=n-r\) and \[ (r^\vee,s^\vee,t^\vee)=(q,n-s,q-s+t). \] Then \(1\le t^\vee\le r^\vee,s^\vee\le n\) and \[ t^\vee>r^\vee+s^\vee-n. \] Indeed, \(t^\vee=q-s+t\ge1\) follows from \(t>r+s-n\); \(t^\vee\le q=r^\vee\) follows from \(t\le s\); \(t^\vee\le n-s=s^\vee\) follows from \(t\le r\); and \[ t^\vee-(r^\vee+s^\vee-n)=t>0. \] The original inequalities also force \(r,s<n\), hence \(r^\vee,s^\vee\ge1\).
- claim-4: The conjugated parameters are \[ i^\vee=s^\vee-t^\vee+1=j,\qquad j^\vee=r^\vee-t^\vee+1=i, \] and consequently \[ a^\vee=\min(n-r^\vee-i^\vee,r^\vee-j^\vee) =\min(r-j,q-i)=a,\qquad b^\vee=b. \]
- claim-5: The original core and both family upper shapes lie in the \(q^r\) box: \[ i\le q,\quad j\le r,\quad i+a\le q,\quad j+a\le r,\quad b\le i,j. \] Here \(q-i=t^\vee-1\ge0\), \(r-j=t-1\ge0\), and the two inequalities involving \(a\) follow from \(a=\min(q-i,r-j)\). The transformed statements are exactly \[ j\le r,\quad i\le q,\quad j+a\le r,\quad i+a\le q,\quad b\le j,i, \] so the transformed lower family is contained in the \(r^q\) box.
- claim-6: Conjugation of partitions gives the exact family correspondence \[ \left\{\lambda:j^i\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(j^i,b^a)\right\}' = \left\{\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\right\}. \] This uses \(b\le i,j\); the transpose of the \(a\times b\) lower adjoinment is an \(a\)-wide right adjoinment in the first \(b\) rows.
- claim-7: If \(a\ge1\) and \(1\le N\le ab\), then both \[ (n,r,i,j,a,b,N),\qquad(n,r^\vee,j,i,a,b,N) \] are valid: positivity is clear, \(r^\vee=q<n\), and the transformed containment conditions are \[ a+i\le q=r^\vee,\qquad a+j\le r=n-r^\vee. \]
- claim-8: The \(a=0\) boundary is excluded from valid tuples, since validity requires \(a\ge1\). Moreover, \[ a=0\iff (q-i=0)\ \text{or}\ (r-j=0) \iff (i=q)\ \text{or}\ (j=r). \] Under parameter conjugation these alternatives interchange. In either case both \(b^a\) adjoinments are empty, so each relevant family is the singleton core; no condition \(1\le N\le ab=0\) can hold.
## Strategy
Put \(q=n-r\). Assume
\[
1\le t\le r,s\le n,\qquad t>r+s-n,
\]
and define
\[
(r^\vee,s^\vee,t^\vee)=(q,n-s,q-s+t).
\]
First \(r,s<n\): if \(r=n\), then \(t>s\), contradicting \(t\le s\); similarly \(s=n\) contradicts \(t\le r\). Thus \(q,r^\vee,s^\vee\ge1\). Moreover
\[
t^\vee=t-(r+s-n)\ge1,\quad
t^\vee\le q\iff t\le s,\quad
t^\vee\le n-s\iff t\le r,
\]
and
\[
t^\vee-(r^\vee+s^\vee-n)=t>0.
\]
Hence the conjugated tuple satisfies all bigrassmannian inequalities.

With
\[
i=s-t+1,\quad j=r-t+1,\quad a=\min(q-i,r-j),\quad b=\min(i,j),
\]
one has
\[
i^\vee=j,\qquad j^\vee=i,\qquad
a^\vee=\min(r-j,q-i)=a,\qquad b^\vee=b.
\]
Also
\[
q-i=t^\vee-1\ge0,\qquad r-j=t-1\ge0,\qquad
a\le q-i,\ r-j,\qquad b\le i,j.
\]

The required shape and box checks are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
\text{ambient box}&\text{shape}&\text{width bound}&\text{height bound}\\ \hline
q^r&i^j&i\le q&j\le r\\
q^r&(i^j,b^a)&i\le q&j+a\le r\\
q^r&((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})&i+a\le q&j\le r\\ \hline
r^q&j^i&j\le r&i\le q\\
r^q&(j^i,b^a)&j\le r&i+a\le q\\
r^q&((j+a)^b,j^{i-b})&j+a\le r&i\le q
\end{array}
\]
Here \(b\le i,j\) ensures that every displayed expression is a partition and that each upper shape contains its indicated core. Consequently every partition in each of the four family intervals lies in its stated ambient box.

Conjugation gives both exact family correspondences:
\[
\{\lambda:i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}'
=
\{\mu:j^i\subseteq\mu\subseteq((j+a)^b,j^{i-b})\},
\]
\[
\{\lambda:i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}'
=
\{\mu:j^i\subseteq\mu\subseteq(j^i,b^a)\}.
\]

If \(a\ge1\) and \(1\le N\le ab\), then both
\[
(n,r,i,j,a,b,N),\qquad(n,q,j,i,a,b,N)
\]
are valid: every coordinate is positive; \(r<n\) and \(q<n\); and
\[
a+j\le r,\quad a+i\le q,\quad b\le i,j,\quad 1\le N\le ab
\]
become respectively
\[
a+j^\vee=a+i\le q=r^\vee,\qquad
a+i^\vee=a+j\le r=n-r^\vee,\qquad
b\le i^\vee,j^\vee,\qquad 1\le N\le ab.
\]

Finally,
\[
a=0\iff q-i=0\ \text{or}\ r-j=0
\iff i=q\ \text{or}\ j=r.
\]
These alternatives interchange under conjugation. In this boundary case,
\[
(i^j,b^0)=((i+0)^b,i^{j-b})=i^j,
\]
and likewise both conjugated upper shapes equal \(j^i\). Thus all four families are singleton cores. Since \(ab=0\), no \(N\) satisfies \(1\le N\le ab\); hence this case is excluded from valid tuples.

The requested standalone admissibility certificate is established. No minimality or parent theorem is inferred.
